Etiquette:

  • Don't drop weights.
  • Don't hog machines/weights for like 45 minutes, sitting playing with your phone. Do your sets and put them back/move on.
  • Don't be afraid to ask for advice or a spot.
  • Wipe down equipment after use.

Tips:

  • Don't load up on weight and put out 1 shitty, jerky rep; I see this waaaay too much. Once you can do 3 sets of 10 smooth, controlled reps then you can add a little extra weight (keep it about 5kg extra at a time, max).
  • Learn to squat low with good form and also dead-lift with good form. These two will strengthen your whole body, but importantly your lower back which may save you some injuries down the line.
  • Free Weights are vastly superior to machines, especially when you get your compound lift game on.
  • Don't neglect the warm up and warm down. 5 mins each at least. A physio or the like can give you some good exercises for this, depending on your particular needs.
  • Don't neglect cardio. Boot Camp or HIT makes a great 'off day' activity IMO.
  • Eat clean. You can't outrun or out-lift a shitty diet. Good nutrition will make exercise much easier.
  • Be Patient. You wont look like Arnie after 1 week, not even 1 year. But you will feel and look much better.

Good on you, this is a great move since keeping your body moving and healthy is critical.

Tips:

  • Define what your purpose is, interested in going big and doing some beautiful squats and deadlifts? Powerlifting might be your thing then, although that doesn't mean you need to aim to get right swole and deadlift 700 lbs or something - there is no problem in shooting for the intermediate level and staying there for the health benefits and enjoyment of lifting
  • Following a program makes things a lot easier, it helps give you direction which I found makes it easier to keep at instead of wandering around the gym wondering what to do next
  • Come up with a goals or milestones, always make it obtainable and chunk away at it in increments. If you do it in incremental steps and succeed it feels good, say you lift x amount of weight now and want to hit x amount say 30 lbs higher once you reach that its a wonderful feeling of success and real progress. This is much more obtainable then doing it in say 100 lbs increments.
  • In the beginning gains actually do happen quickly, at least relevative to what it later becomes, but don't get detered if things are not progressing fast enough - focus on the long haul in a sustainable manner and you will get there
  • Watch people who are better then you, you can always gain valuable knowledge from watching and listening to people who are far into it. An example, you see a guy squating heavy with immaculate form watch very carefully there are a lot of subtle queues and techniques in use so by watching you can learn and incorporate what you have learnt into your form thus improving your lift which works you towards the milestones you hopefully set for yourself
  • In the beginning the pain is real, it sucks badly starting out since you body is adjusting and there is lots of recovery going on. Know that as you keep at it this does mostly go away, while you still get doms from a good workout its not agony like in the beginning plus you just get used to it so a bit of soreness becomes less of a deal
  • If you notice yourself getting knots in your quads or anywhere it can be very benefical to get a foam roller for when you are home. You can use it to work the knots out and do it while you're watching a movie even
  • Stretch before lifting, depending what you're doing what and how you stretch will differ but in the end it will help you preform best and avoid injury
  • Speaking of avoiding injury, when you're lifting your should be 'ramping up' to your working weight as part of your warm up. Start with the bar and work your way up, with my deadlift I'll start with the bar doing a set and then go 135, 225, 315 then add on the rest depending what the day calls for so on my heavy day (more weight, less reps, currently do 1x5 on heavy day) I work at 355 lbs

Etiquette:

  • Clean your weights and bars
  • Put your weights and plates away
  • If someone looks like they are watting for a bench or rack let them know how many sets you have left or even offer to take turns. This can be a good opportunity to meet someone, get a spotter, gain some tips etc
  • Don't rest too long, by too long thats meant approx 5 mins, it hogs the equipment and harms your work out

td lr; go fucking lift, dont be a cunt, clean up after yourself, take your time and settle in for the long haul, focus on form, set your expectations, enjoy the work out and the jouney, the pain gets better
